The main takeaway from our work is that

the MAC layer should be able to control the number of competing stations in each access category (AC), which is the key to maximizing the network throughput and achieving proportional bandwidth sharing.

the number of competing stations is not an appropriate metric to control contention in WLANs, and the key to contention control lies in controlling the effective number of stations competing for access.

, in the design of a contention control scheme for IEEE 802.1e WLAN, it is more effective to focus on the control of the effective number of contending nodes than on estimating the actual number of contending stations.
